messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: tenant=BrightMed SLA_violation detected (p95 latency > 3s) for 6m across region=us-west-2. Triggering paging policy: P1.
Alex P: ack. I'm on it. Pulling up graphs.
Mira S: saw a spike too, looks like a migration batch from BrightMed started ~10:18 UTC. High cardinality on per-tenant check.
Samir K: can we silence the per-tenant dense check while we triage? It's spamming the pager for similar tenants.
Alex P: yes, plan: 1) silence the BrightMed-specific alert for 30m, 2) add debounce on the per-tenant check, 3) create a per-tenant aggregate SLO check (weighted) to avoid noisy single-host spikes.
Jules R: +1. Also add a guard that an alert only fires if p95>3s AND error_rate>0.5% — we had a lot of transient latency without user impact.
Ops Oncall: temporary silence command: 
```
opsctl silence --check tenant-p95-latency --tenant BrightMed --duration 30m --reason "investigating migration-induced spike"
```
Incident Bot: Silence applied by Ops Oncall until 30m from now.
Alex P: looking at host-level traces: BrightMed batch job hit a downstream vector-db causing retries and latency amplification. Pattern: many small requests in tight loop.
Mira S: Confirmed. Downstream service vecstore-us-west had a GC pause at ~10:16 that coincides. We should tag this as downstream-induced.
Samir K: For alert tuning: propose changing rule from "per-tenant p95 > 3s for 5m" to "per-tenant p95 > 3s for 5m AND per-tenant request_count > 1000 in window" — reduces noise from low-volume tenants.
Jules R: Also propose adding a rolling-debounce: only fire if condition holds in 3/5 windows of 1m, instead of strict contiguous 5m. That handles jittery infra.
Alex P: I'll push an opsplaybook entry and a one-off Grafana dashboard panel for BrightMed showing p50/p95/p99 + downstream latencies + retry rates.
Mira S: can we add a metric to the check that groups by workload_type so we don't get breaks from admin jobs? e.g., exclude jobs tagged "maintenance".
Samir K: Good idea. We'll filter by tag and by request path prefix.
Ops Oncall: filed ticket RH-3421 to make alert changes (owner: Samir, due: EOD). Also created dashboard note: DB-Quicklook-BrightMed.
Alex P: handing off to next oncall in 25m. Summary for handoff: BrightMed spike traced to vecstore GC causing retries -> per-tenant alerts are noisy for low-volume spikes -> applied 30m silence -> follow-ups: RH-3421 (alert rule changes), RH-3422 (dashboard panel), RH-3423 (runbook update).
Jules R: FYI we should consider a global policy: if >3 tenants in last hour cause alerts with same downstream signature, auto-escalate to infra rather than mute per-tenant.
Mira S: logged that as RH-3424.
Incident Bot: @Alex P marked the incident as "mitigated" at 10:46 UTC by applying silence and coordinating follow-ups.
Samir K: I'll own the alert rule PR, will post the PR link here when ready.
Ops Oncall: next oncall: @Mira S, @Jules R — please take over monitoring for the next 30m and ensure no regression after silence expires.
Mira S: taking it. Will watch the new dashboard and confirm silence expiry.
Alex P: thanks all. Quick note for postmortem: this is an alert-tuning + downstream reliability item, not a serving outage. Suggest post-incident action: add tenant-level debounce, threshold by request volume, exclude maintenance job tags, and add a per-downstream fingerprint to reduce noisy pages.
Jules R: Agreed. I'll draft the post-incident doc and include the snippets and opsctl commands.
Samir K: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/ops-alerts/pull/198 (WIP).
Mira S: once PR merges, schedule a 1h runbook update session next week.
Ops Oncall: closing thread for now. Reopen if BrightMed shows new alerts after silence. :wave:
